purpose: Heavy Rebuild v2 clean-master architectural and service program for the authoritative ruined gas station asset, preserving a legible roadside retail-fuel site with canopy, pump islands, underground or protected fuel storage, convenience retail, service access, vehicle circulation, safety systems, terrain seating and coherent damage behavior.
ground_program: roadside entrance and exit geometry supports passenger vehicles and light service traffic without forcing unrealistic turns across pump islands or pedestrian approaches
fuel forecourt contains multiple protected pump islands connected to a credible buried or protected fuel-delivery system rather than isolated decorative dispensers
canopy covers the principal fueling positions and uses columns, foundations and beam relationships that visibly support the roof without obstructing required vehicle clearances
fuel storage is represented by buried tanks, protected above-ground tanks or another plausible system with fill points, vents, inspection access and a believable connection to the dispensing network
convenience-store or cashier building includes public sales space, counter, storage, staff/service area, sanitation and back-of-house access appropriate to a roadside fuel retailer
delivery and refuse access reaches the store and fuel-service systems without requiring trucks to occupy the primary customer fueling path for normal operations
emergency shutoff, fire extinguishing, spill-response and vehicle-impact protection are located where they would plausibly protect pumps, storefronts and fuel infrastructure
signage, price-board base, lighting supports, curbs, drainage and edge treatments reinforce the site identity without becoming unsupported decorative clutter
service access reaches pumps, tank fill points, vents, canopy systems, electrical equipment and store utilities without relying on inaccessible maintenance spaces
grading, curbs, drainage, retaining features and slab transitions seat the forecourt and store into terrain without floating paving, buried doors or disconnected road elevations
upper_program: the canopy roof preserves supported spans, drainage and maintenance access while avoiding impossible unsupported overhangs
store roof equipment, vents or small service platforms remain structurally supported and reachable by plausible maintenance access
any occupied mezzanine or second-floor space uses a supported enclosed stair and usable landing rather than ladders intended for equipment access
pole signs, lighting and elevated branding structures use foundations and mast or frame logic sufficient for their visible height and wind exposure
circulation: customer vehicles can enter, choose a pump position, maneuver around occupied islands and exit without unavoidable conflicts with the store entrance or delivery zone
pedestrian circulation connects parking and pump areas to the store entrance using protected or legible paths across the forecourt
staff circulation connects sales floor, counter, storage, sanitation, service yard and utility access without requiring passage through hazardous fuel-service zones
fuel-delivery access reaches tank fill points while preserving a plausible tanker position and minimizing blockage of the entire customer forecourt
maintenance circulation reaches dispensers, canopy supports, electrical equipment, vents, fill points and drainage features
equipment-only ladders do not substitute for architectural stairs in occupied spaces
damage_constraints: the ruined derivative must remain immediately recognizable as a gas station through surviving pump-island, canopy, storefront, fuel-storage and roadside-sign relationships
favor localized canopy collapse, vehicle impact, pump fire, storefront breach, roof failure, fuel staining, broken glazing, corrosion, vandalism and vegetation intrusion over uniform random deletion
canopy collapse must follow gravity from failed columns, beams or roof sections and resolve attached lights, signs, gutters and fascia so floating fragments are not left behind

pump or fuel-system damage may include scorched islands, displaced dispensers, ruptured housings or spill evidence but should retain enough of the distribution layout to communicate the site's former function
store damage should preserve at least one legible public-to-counter-to-back-of-house relationship and one viable exploration route
road, forecourt, curbs and drainage should remain spatially coherent after damage rather than becoming an arbitrary field of disconnected slabs
derive damaged, occupied or contaminated variants only from this immutable clean master
